# Tabs — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for tabs when the content is genuinely parallel — the same thing seen from several angles, like a conversation's messages, details and files. Give each tab a short noun label and keep the number small enough that no label is hidden behind a scroll. Tabs are not navigation: if the panels are really different places with their own URLs, use links and let people bookmark them. Keep a panel's content independent of the others, so switching back does not lose what someone typed.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use primary tabs under the top app bar for main destinations.
- Keep one tab active; every tab references its panel via aria-controls.
- Label icon-only tabs for assistive tech.

**Don't**

- Don't mix primary and secondary tabs in one bar.
- Don't use tabs for navigation away — tabs switch views, they never leave.
- Don't use fewer than three tabs — use segmented buttons or plain text.

| Inactive label | hover | comp.primary-tab.inactive-hover | on-surface + 8% layer |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| TabsRoot | Owns which tab is selected. Accepts `value`/`onValueChange` to control it. |
| TabsList | The row of tab triggers. Handles the arrow-key roving focus between them. |
| TabsTab | One trigger. Carries the selected state and the indicator. |
| TabsPanel | The content for one tab, kept in the DOM only while selected. |

### FAQ

**Primary or secondary?**

Primary under the app bar for main destinations (3px indicator, primary active text). Secondary inside content for sub-sections (2px indicator, on-surface active text).

## Native

### Features

Reach for a tabs when the alternatives are peers — different views of one record, different facets of one list — and any of them could reasonably be first. Each tab is data with a `value`, a `label` and optional `content`, and the group reports the selected `value`. The content riding on the tab is the useful part: it means the tab and what it shows are declared together, so they cannot drift apart. If the steps have an order and someone must do them in sequence, that is a stepper, not tabs.

### Usage

**Do**

- Declare tabs as data — `value`, `label`, optional `content` — so the set is one declaration.
- Keep labels to one or two words; a tab is a signpost, not a sentence.
- Drive `value`/`onValueChange` when the tab must follow app state (deep links, wizards); leave uncontrolled otherwise.

**Don't**

- Don't use tabs for a binary choice — that is a segmented button or switch.
- Don't change the tab count after mount — the set is the navigation, not content.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active tab label | selected | theme.color.primary | primary label on the selected tab |
| Inactive tab label | resting | theme.color.onSurfaceVariant | onSurfaceVariant label, minHeight 48 per tab |
| Active indicator | selected | theme.color.primary | 3px primary underline under the selected tab |
| Bar divider | resting | theme.color.outlineVariant | 1px outlineVariant rule under the bar |

### FAQ

**Tabs or segmented button?**

Tabs switch views or panels (content follows the tab); a segmented button switches a value within one view. Navigation means tabs.

**How does this differ from the web tabs?**

The contract is the same (data-declared set, controlled or uncontrolled). Both mark selection with the primary treatment plus the screen-reader `selected` state.
